title: US markets closed — Christmas Day (removes a session from the year's last full trading week)
source: EST: derived by statute and weekday arithmetic, computed mechanically by this session, not read off an exchange calendar. 5 U.S.C. 6103 fixes Christmas Day as a legal public holiday on December 25; December 25 2026 falls on a FRIDAY, so it is observed on the day itself with no Friday-to-Thursday or Saturday-to-Friday shift, and the NYSE closes for the full session. Corroborated inside this repo rather than from an outside fetch, and the corroboration is circumstantial by construction: the calendar already carries christmas-eve-half-day-2026-12-24 ('US equity markets close early at 1:00 p.m. ET — Christmas Eve'), an entry whose existence presupposes the 12-25 closure, since the NYSE schedules an early close only on the eve of a full holiday. NO EXCHANGE CALENDAR WAS FETCHED for this proposal — the remote session egress proxy blocks nyse.com and sifma.org outright (docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md, Honesty rules), which is the same limit labor-day-market-closure-2026-09-07 worked around with a Treasury auction series and this proposal did not attempt. Filed estimate on three counts: no primary exchange source was read, the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no slot for an exchange's own holiday calendar (the reason every sibling closure entry is estimate), and this lane never self-confirms an event it discovered in-sweep. The DATE is not in doubt; the estimate label is about the sourcing, not the evidence. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: PROPOSED by the sp-select-sector-secondary-reweight-2026-12-31 initial research (2026-09-08), which found it by counting the trading sessions in its own reset-to-test drift window (2026-12-18 close → 2026-12-30) and noticing the calendar had no entry for the closure that removes one of them. THE GAP IS PATTERNED, NOT ISOLATED: this calendar tracks US closures elsewhere in the sequence — labor-day-market-closure-2026-09-07, good-friday-market-closure-2027-03-26, memorial-day-market-closure-2027-05-31, thanksgiving-market-closure-2027-11-25, christmas-market-closure-2027-12-24 (proposed) — and tracks the 2026 HALF days (thanksgiving-half-day-2026-11-27, christmas-eve-half-day-2026-12-24) while carrying neither of the 2026 full closures they precede. thanksgiving-market-closure-2026-11-26 is the same omission and is NOT filed here: it sits outside this proposer's corridor, so filing it would be scope creep, and it is recorded as an observation for whichever lane's sweep next reaches it. WHAT THE RESEARCHING LANE SHOULD DO FIRST: fetch a primary schedule this session could not — nyse.com/markets/hours-calendars is egress-blocked, but the Treasury auction series at api.fiscaldata.treasury.gov is not, and the labor-day-market-closure-2026-09-07 entry demonstrates the technique (a bill auction slate shifted off its usual weekday is mechanical third-party proof of a closure). Low impact: a scheduled full closure known a year ahead moves no price and licenses nothing; its only value is that flow arithmetic across the year-end corridor counts sessions correctly. Kind sector matches every sibling closure entry — the imperfect enum fit for a market-structure event is named, not fixed from this lane.
